SECURITY & DATA OWNERSHIP

Your data is yours. Here’s exactly how we keep it that way.

A family business’s customer list is its most valuable asset. Here is what protects it in plain words first, then the technical depth, and what we are still building, stated plainly.

You’re probably asking

In short

How does Jwero protect a jeweller’s data?

Every business runs in its own isolated database, with encryption, role-based access, approval queues and limits on what AI can do. You set backup frequency and retention, can export your data at any time, and can ask for the latest restore check for your workspace.

THE SHIFT

From a vendor holding your data to owning it outright.

Today

Customer data sits in whichever tool captured it, exportable only if the vendor allows.

Gone with Jwero

Hostage data and the fear of what happens if you leave.

At the speed of thought

Every business in its own isolated database, exportable any time, with role-based access your team controls.

Ask the vendorExport yourself

IN PLAIN WORDS

For everyone, not just IT.

Where your data lives

One isolated database per business. Your data lives alone, encrypted, never mixed with anyone else’s.

Who can see what

Role-based access, per role and per branch. Owner, manager and counter staff see different worlds.

Export anytime

Your data leaves with you in standard formats whenever you ask. No hostage clauses.

What AI can and can’t do

Every AI action waits in an approval queue inside caps and quiet hours you set, never a surprise message.

Approvals on money

Maker-checker approvals and tamper-evident document trails on financial records.

Kill switches

Pause any AI activity instantly, at five scopes, one action, one agent, one branch, one channel, or everything.

THE TECHNICAL LAYER

For your IT evaluator.

HostingMicrosoft Azure, India region. Providers that process data elsewhere are listed on the Sub-processors page.
Tenant isolationOne database per business, physical isolation, not row-level flags.
EncryptionEncrypted credentials; data encrypted in transit and at rest.
AuthenticationMulti-factor authentication and passkeys; enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC) with SCIM provisioning for chain deployments; sessions revocable globally in one action.
Access controlRole-based access control, ~150 fine-grained permission slugs, fail-closed checker.
AI authorisationA second permission axis for AI: per-user/org action allowlists, independent of human RBAC.
Financial integrityMaker-checker approvals and tamper-evident document transitions on financial records.
Activity recordsWho did what is logged per module and kept for up to 12 months. Exports of customer or employee data are recorded.
Personal data requestsExport and erasure of a customer’s or an employee’s record from inside the product, with statutory records retained.
AI and your dataAI features send the content needed for a draft to the model providers named on the Sub-processors page. Jwero does not train its own models on your records.
IncidentsA written incident response plan. If your data is affected you are told without undue delay.
Reporting a vulnerabilityWrite to care@jwero.ai with the subject “Security”. We acknowledge within two working days and will not pursue anyone who reports in good faith.

WHAT WE DON'T DO YET

Here's what's on the public roadmap, not the product, said plainly, before you find out the hard way.

  • Formal certifications: ISO 27001 and SOC 2 are in progress, not certified; published only when earned.
  • A single unified, immutable audit trail across every module, activity logging exists per module today; consolidation is in progress.
See the full public roadmap →

COMPLIANCE

Where our compliance documentation lives.

The full set is public: the Privacy Policy, the Terms of Use, the Data Policy (ownership, processing terms, retention, export and breach notification), the Sub-processors list and the DPDP statement.

Download the security overview (PDF) Ask a follow-up

THE FEARS OWNERS DON’T ALWAYS SAY OUT LOUD

Questions owners ask us privately.

This is family business data: how do I know it won’t leave the family?

It runs in a database isolated to your business alone. Nobody outside your business can see it, and that isolation is built in, not promised.

What happens to customer data if a salesperson leaves?

Deactivate their login in seconds. Every record stays with the business, because it was always the business’s record and never the individual’s.

What if the internet goes down at my shop?

Honestly: Jwero needs a connection today. Offline mode is on the roadmap, not shipped.

Can a competitor of mine, also on Jwero, see my data?

No. Database-per-tenant isolation means it structurally cannot happen, regardless of who else uses the platform.
